Study cases reflect the capabilities of current, commercial technologies at scales representative of next commercial offerings facing no fundamental research, development, and demonstration obstacles. Three natural gas (NG) to ammonia plant configurations, with and without carbon dioxide capture and storage (CCS), were analyzed using technoeconomic analysis. The plant site was selected to be a generic location in the U.S. Midwest with CO transport and storage (T&S) in the Illinois Basin. A 2 summary of the plant configurations is shown in Exhibit ES-1. QGESS guidance was followed where applicable, with changes or clarifications noted. This ensures sound, consistent, and transparent technology assessments and comparisons within and across NETL studies. Aspen Plus® (Aspen) models were developed for the three natural gas reforming to ammonia configurations. The models were used to generate energy and mass balances, which were used as the basis for generating the capital and operating cost estimates. Performance data were based upon published reports, information obtained from vendors and users of the technology, performance data from design/build projects, and engineering judgment. Most capital and operating costs were estimated by scaling costs available from prior studies using NETL QGESS methodology. Select capital and consumable costs were provided by Black & Veatch. All costs are in January-2023 dollars. The capital and operation and maintenance (O&M) costs for each of the cases were estimated using a scaling approach using reference costs from prior NETL studies according to the 2024 revision of the QGESS document “Capital Cost Scaling Methodology: Revision 4b Report” (NETL, 2025a).
